title: The Cascade and Inheritance
description: Understand how the Cascade reconciles Origin, Specificity, and Source Order; how inheritable properties flow down the DOM tree; and how to write maintainable overrides without reaching for !important.

objectives.statement: Resolve styling conflicts using the Cascade hierarchy: Importance, Origin, Specificity, and Source Order.
Apply inheritable CSS properties to parent containers and predict which properties cascade to descendant elements.

content.title: The Cascade & Downward Inheritance
content.hook: The 'C' in CSS stands for Cascading. Styles cascade like a waterfall from parent to child, and when rules collide, a strict set of tiebreaker laws determines the winner.
content.context: When specificity is equal, Source Order is the final tiebreaker: the last rule defined in the CSS wins. Meanwhile, properties related to typography (like `color`, `font-family`, `line-height`) are inherited by children automatically, while layout properties (like `border`, `margin`, `padding`) are not.
goals: Distinguish inherited properties (typography) from non-inherited properties (box model).
Structure style sheets cleanly without relying on `!important` overrides.

content.title: The Cascade Tiebreaker Algorithm
content.description: Conflict Resolution Order: 1. Importance (!important) → 2. Specificity (Inline > ID > Class > Tag) → 3. Source Order (Last declaration wins). Inheritance flows down text nodes.

content.prompt:
Given the two CSS rules below targeting `.alert` with equal specificity, what text color is applied to `
Warning
`?
options: orange (the first rule defined locks the property)
red (the later declaration wins because specificity is tied)

validation.expected: red (the later declaration wins because specificity is tied)

feedback.correct: Correct! When origin and specificity are identical, the Cascade falls back to Source Order: declarations lower down in the file override earlier ones.
feedback.incorrect: When specificity is identical, the Cascade applies the declaration that appears last in the stylesheet source order. Red wins.

content.title: Leverage Inheritance and Order
content.prompt:
Write CSS rules to style the container and descendants:
1. Set `color: #334155` and `font-family: sans-serif` on `.card` so all text inside inherits it.
2. In a separate rule, override the `.special-note` element to have `color: #dc2626`.
3. Add a second rule for `.card` later in the style tag that sets `background-color: #f8fafc`.

content.prompt: Why is slapping `!important` onto a CSS rule considered an anti-pattern in collaborative production codebases?

feedback.correct: Spot on! `!important` breaks the natural specificity cascade, making future overrides impossible without adding more `!important` declarations, creating unmaintainable specificity debt.
feedback.incorrect: Consider how `!important` affects teammates trying to override a style later or build variants of a component.

content.title: Key Takeaways: Cascade & Inheritance
takeaways: The Cascade resolves conflicts through Importance, Specificity, and Source Order.
When specificity is tied, the rule declared latest in the stylesheet wins.
Typography properties (color, font-family, font-size) naturally inherit down the DOM tree.
Layout properties (border, padding, margin) do not inherit.
Avoid !important by writing clean, low-specificity class-based selectors.
